complications.name: Cardiovascular disease
complications.source_text: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a broad term that includes atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and heart failure, two CVDs common among people with diabetes (1).

complications.name: Heart failure
complications.source_text: CVD also includes heart failure, and diabetes is a risk factor for incident heart failure, which is at least twofold more prevalent in people with diabetes compared with those without diabetes and is a major cause of morbidity and mortality (11). People with diabetes may present with a wide spectrum of heart failure, including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF), or heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (12,13).

complications.name: Chronic kidney disease
complications.source_text: There is an increasing appreciation of the common pathophysiology and interrelationship of cardiometabolic risk factors leading to both adverse cardiovascular and adverse kidney outcomes in people with diabetes, including ASCVD, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease (CKD) (17,18).

complications.name: Hypertension
complications.source_text: An elevated blood pressure is defined as a systolic blood pressure 120–129 mmHg with a diastolic blood pressure <80 mmHg (23). Hypertension is defined as a systolic blood pressure ≥130 mmHg or a diastolic blood pressure ≥80 mmHg (23).

complications.name: Peripheral artery disease
complications.source_text: ASCVD broadly refers to a history of acute coronary syndrome, myocardial infarction (MI), stable or unstable angina or coronary or other arterial revascularization, stroke, or peripheral artery disease (PAD) including aortic aneurysm and is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in people with diabetes (1).

complications.name: Acute kidney injury
complications.source_text: AKI is defined as a rapid decline in kidney function, typically within a short period (hours to days), characterized by increase in serum creatinine and/or decrease in urine output (80).

complications.name: Hyperkalemia
complications.source_text: Treatment with ACE inhibitors and ARBs or MRAs can cause AKI and hyperkalemia, while diuretics can cause AKI and either hypokalemia or hyperkalemia (depending on mechanism of action) (77,78).

complications.name: Hypotension
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Syncope
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Bradycardia
complications.source_text: Adverse events attributed to blood pressure treatment, including hypotension, syncope, bradycardia, hyperkalemia, and elevations in serum creatinine, occurred more frequently in the intensive treatment arm than in the standard therapy arm.

complications.name: Statin intolerance
complications.source_text: Statin therapy is a cornerstone of CVD prevention and treatment; however, a subset of individuals experience partial (inability to tolerate sufficient dosage necessary to achieve therapeutic objectives due to adverse effects) or complete (inability to tolerate any dose) intolerance to statin therapy (127).

complications.name: Musculoskeletal adverse effects
complications.source_text: Fewer musculoskeletal adverse effects occurred in those treated with evolocumab or ezetimibe than in those treated with ezetimibe plus placebo, although rates of discontinuation due to these effects were similar.

complications.name: Bleeding
complications.source_text: In contrast, major bleeding was significantly increased from 3.2 to 4.1% in the aspirin group (rate ratio 1.29; P = 0.003), with most of the excess being gastrointestinal bleeding and other extracranial bleeding.

complications.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
complications.source_text: Diabetic ketoacidosis and euglycemic ketoacidosis (266).

complications.name: Euglycemic ketoacidosis
complications.source_text: Diabetic ketoacidosis and euglycemic ketoacidosis (266).

complications.name: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
complications.source_text: In people with type 2 diabetes and established heart failure with either preserved or reduced ejection fraction, an SGLT2 inhibitor with proven benefit in this population is recommended to improve quality of life. A

complications.name: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
complications.source_text: In people with type 2 diabetes and established heart failure with either preserved or reduced ejection fraction, an SGLT2 inhibitor with proven benefit in this population is recommended to improve quality of life. A

complications.name: Heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction
complications.source_text: People with diabetes may present with a wide spectrum of heart failure, including heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF), or heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (12,13).

complications.name: Albuminuria
complications.source_text: An ACE inhibitor (ACEi) or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) is suggested for the treatment of hypertension in people with coronary artery disease (CAD) or urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 30–299 mg/g creatinine and is strongly recommended for individuals with urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥300 mg/g creatinine. †Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (CCB). ‡Thiazide-like diuretic; long-acting agents shown to reduce cardiovascular events, such as chlorthalidone and indapamide, are preferred. §If it can be safely attained, the on-treatment blood pressure goal is <130/80 mmHg; a systolic blood pressure goal <120 mmHg should be encouraged in individuals with high cardiovascular or kidney risk. BP, blood pressure. Adapted from de Boer et al. (24).

screening_tests.name: Blood pressure measurement
screening_tests.source_text: Blood pressure should be measured at every routine clinical visit, or at least every 6 months by a trained individual who should follow the guidelines established for the general population: measurement in the seated position, with feet on the floor and arm supported at heart level, after 5 min of rest. Cuff size should be appropriate for the upper-arm circumference (29).
screening_tests.frequency: every routine clinical visit, or at least every 6 months

screening_tests.name: Home blood pressure self-monitoring
screening_tests.source_text: Home blood pressure self-monitoring and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring may provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure (30,31).
screening_tests.indication: To provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure

screening_tests.name: 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
screening_tests.source_text: Home blood pressure self-monitoring and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure monitoring may provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure (30,31).
screening_tests.indication: To provide evidence of white coat hypertension, masked hypertension, or other discrepancies between office and true blood pressure

screening_tests.name: Lipid profile
screening_tests.source_text: In adults with prediabetes or diabetes not taking statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, it is reasonable to obtain a lipid profile at the time of diagnosis, at an initial medical evaluation, annually thereafter, or more frequently if indicated. E
screening_tests.frequency: at the time of diagnosis, at an initial medical evaluation, annually thereafter, or more frequently if indicated
screening_tests.indication: Adults with prediabetes or diabetes not taking statins or other lipid-lowering therapy

screening_tests.name: Lipid profile
screening_tests.source_text: Obtain a lipid profile at initiation of statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, 4–12 weeks after initiation or a change in dose, and annually thereafter, as it facilitates monitoring the response to therapy and informs medication-taking behavior. A
screening_tests.frequency: at initiation of statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, 4–12 weeks after initiation or a change in dose, and annually thereafter
screening_tests.indication: Initiation of statins or other lipid-lowering therapy

screening_tests.name: Ankle-brachial index testing
screening_tests.source_text: In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, screening for PAD with ankle-brachial index testing is recommended if a PAD diagnosis would change management. B
screening_tests.indication: Asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, if a PAD diagnosis would change management

screening_tests.name: Natriuretic peptide measurement
screening_tests.source_text: Adults with diabetes are at increased risk for the development of asymptomatic cardiac structural or functional abnormalities (stage B heart failure) or symptomatic (stage C) heart failure. Consider screening adults with diabetes by measuring a natriuretic peptide (B-type natriuretic peptide [BNP] or N-terminal pro-BNP [NT-proBNP]) to facilitate prevention of stage C heart failure.
screening_tests.indication: Adults with diabetes to facilitate prevention of stage C heart failure

screening_tests.name: Echocardiography
screening_tests.source_text: In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and abnormal natriuretic peptide levels, echocardiography is recommended to identify stage B heart failure. A
screening_tests.indication: Asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and abnormal natriuretic peptide levels

screening_tests.name: Coronary artery calcium measurement
screening_tests.source_text: In adults with diabetes ≥40 years of age, measurement of coronary artery calcium is also reasonable for cardiovascular risk assessment.
screening_tests.indication: Adults with diabetes ≥40 years of age for cardiovascular risk assessment

screening_tests.name: Exercise ECG testing
screening_tests.source_text: Exercise ECG testing without or with echocardiography may be used as the initial test.
screening_tests.indication: Candidates for advanced or invasive cardiac testing with symptoms or signs of cardiac or vascular disease and an abnormal resting electrocardiogram (ECG)

screening_tests.name: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography
screening_tests.source_text: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography or nuclear imaging should be considered in individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing (e.g., left bundle branch block or ST-T abnormalities).
screening_tests.indication: Individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing

screening_tests.name: Nuclear imaging
screening_tests.source_text: Pharmacologic stress echocardiography or nuclear imaging should be considered in individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing (e.g., left bundle branch block or ST-T abnormalities).
screening_tests.indication: Individuals with diabetes in whom resting ECG abnormalities preclude exercise stress testing

therapeutic_agents.source_text: treatment with SGLT inhibitors and/or GLP-1 RAs that have demonstrated cardiovascular and kidney benefit is considered a fundamental element of risk reduction and a core pharmacological strategy to improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes (Fig. 10.1).

therapeutic_agents.source_text: In individuals with type 2 diabetes and CKD with albuminuria treated with maximum tolerated doses of ACE inhibitor or ARB, recommend treatment with a nonsteroidal MRA with demonstrated benefit to improve cardiovascular outcomes and reduce the risk of CKD progression. A

therapeutic_agents.name: Statin therapy
therapeutic_agents.source_text: For people with diabetes aged 40–75 years without ASCVD, use moderate-intensity statin therapy in addition to lifestyle therapy. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Primary prevention in people with diabetes aged 40–75 years without ASCVD

therapeutic_agents.name: Bempedoic acid
therapeutic_agents.source_text: In people with diabetes intolerant to statin therapy, treatment with bempedoic acid is recommended to reduce cardiovascular event rates as an alternative cholesterol-lowering plan. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: People with diabetes intolerant to statin therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: Ezetimibe
therapeutic_agents.source_text: In people with diabetes and ASCVD, treatment with high-intensity statin therapy is recommended to obtain an LDL cholesterol reduction of ≥50% from baseline and an LDL cholesterol goal of <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L). Addition of ezetimibe or a PCSK9 inhibitor with proven benefit in this population is recommended if this goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy. B
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: People with diabetes and ASCVD if LDL goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: PCSK9 inhibitor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: In people with diabetes and ASCVD, treatment with high-intensity statin therapy is recommended to obtain an LDL cholesterol reduction of ≥50% from baseline and an LDL cholesterol goal of <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L). Addition of ezetimibe or a PCSK9 inhibitor with proven benefit in this population is recommended if this goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy. B
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: People with diabetes and ASCVD if LDL goal is not achieved on maximum tolerated statin therapy

therapeutic_agents.name: Icosapent ethyl
therapeutic_agents.source_text: For individuals with ASCVD or other cardiovascular risk factors on a statin with managed LDL cholesterol but elevated triglycerides (150–499 mg/dL [1.7–5.6 mmol/L]), the addition of icosapent ethyl can be considered to reduce cardiovascular risk. B
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Individuals with ASCVD or other cardiovascular risk factors on a statin with managed LDL cholesterol but elevated triglycerides (150–499 mg/dL [1.7–5.6 mmol/L])

therapeutic_agents.name: Aspirin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Use aspirin therapy (75–162 mg/day) as a secondary prevention strategy in those with diabetes and a history of ASCVD. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Secondary prevention in those with diabetes and a history of ASCVD

therapeutic_agents.name: Clopidogrel
therapeutic_agents.source_text: For individuals with ASCVD and documented aspirin allergy, clopidogrel (75 mg/day) should be used. B
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Individuals with ASCVD and documented aspirin allergy

therapeutic_agents.name: Ticagrelor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Evidence supports use of either ticagrelor or clopidogrel if a percutaneous coronary intervention was performed (187).
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Percutaneous coronary intervention

therapeutic_agents.name: Rivaroxaban
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Combination therapy with 81 mg aspirin daily plus 2.5 mg rivaroxaban twice daily should be considered for individuals with stable coronary and/or peripheral artery disease (PAD) and low bleeding risk to prevent major adverse limb and cardiovascular events. A
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Individuals with stable coronary and/or peripheral artery disease (PAD) and low bleeding risk

therapeutic_agents.name: Finerenone

therapeutic_agents.name: Empagliflozin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: Results of large cardiovascular outcome trials of empagliflozin (10 mg or 25 mg daily) and canagliflozin (100 or 300 mg daily) showed that treatment with either drug reduced rates of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To reduce rates of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death

therapeutic_agents.name: Canagliflozin

therapeutic_agents.name: Dapagliflozin
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The major cardiovascular outcome trial of dapagliflozin (10 mg daily) did not show a reduction in the coprimary outcome of MI, stroke, or cardiovascular death but did show a significantly lower rate of the co-primary composite outcome of hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death, which was driven by its effect on hospitalization for heart failure.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: To reduce hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death

therapeutic_agents.name: Linagliptin

therapeutic_agents.name: SGLT2 inhibitor
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The SGLT2 inhibitors empagliflozin, canagliflozin, and dapagliflozin reduce the incidence of heart failure and improve heart failure–related outcomes, including hospitalization for heart failure and heart failure–related symptoms, in people with diabetes with preserved or reduced ejection fraction (242,247,248,281,286–294).

therapeutic_agents.name: Spironolactone
therapeutic_agents.source_text: The selective nonsteroidal MRA finerenone was examined in the Study to Evaluate the Efficacy (Effect on Disease) and Safety of Finerenone in Participants With Heart Failure and Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (Proportion of Blood Expelled Per Heart Stroke) Greater or Equal to 40% (FINEARTS-HF) trial of people with symptomatic HFpEF (ejection fraction ≥40%) and was found to reduce the risk of total number of worsening heart failure events or cardiovascular death by 16% (rate ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.74–0.95) (303). Of the enrolled participants, 41% had type 2 diabetes. Thus, finerenone improves cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in people with type 2 diabetes. Addition of finerenone can be considered to improve heart failure outcomes in individuals with symptomatic HFpEF. In people with type 2 diabetes and CKD with albuminuria treated with maximum tolerated doses of ACE inhibitor or ARB, the addition of finerenone should be considered to improve cardiovascular outcomes, including the risk for heart failure hospitalization, and to reduce the risk of CKD progression.
therapeutic_agents.when_to_use: Symptomatic HFpEF (ejection fraction ≥40%); people with type 2 diabetes and CKD with albuminuria treated with maximum tolerated doses of ACE inhibitor or ARB
